summary:
Program Description – Astronaut Health Monitoring System
The Astronaut Health Monitoring System is a smart web-based application designed to monitor and protect astronauts' health during space missions. Astronauts face several health challenges in space, such as radiation exposure, dehydration, sleep problems, mental stress, changes in blood pressure, and bone loss due to microgravity.
This program provides a digital health dashboard that continuously displays the health conditions of astronauts using simulated real-time data. It monitors important health parameters such as heart rate, blood pressure, oxygen level, body temperature, breathing rate, sleep duration, and mental stress. It also tracks radiation exposure and changes in body fluids.
The system automatically checks health readings every 15 seconds and identifies possible health problems. It classifies health conditions into three levels: Normal, Warning, and Critical. Based on the detected problems, it provides useful suggestions and safety recommendations for astronauts. It also displays health updates, previous readings, and radiation-related information to help understand changes in health conditions.
The main aim of this project is to provide an easy and effective way to observe astronauts' health, identify risks early, and support quick medical decisions during space missions. This prototype can help improve astronaut safety and support future space exploration.
details:
1. CrewHealth is an astronaut health-monitoring system designed to improve the safety of astronauts during space missions.
  2. It monitors important health parameters such as heart rate, blood pressure, oxygen levels, temperature and mental stress.
  3. It also focuses on space-related health problems such as radiation exposure, dehydration, bone loss and muscle weakness.
  4. The system uses a dashboard to display health information in a simple and understandable format.
  5. It uses colour-coded alerts to identify normal, warning and critical health conditions.
  6. It provides useful recommendations to help astronauts respond to potential health problems.
  7. Our project was developed using HTML, CSS and JavaScript.
  8. We used simulated data to demonstrate the monitoring process without requiring physical sensors.
  9. The main benefit is early identification of health risks and improved medical decision-making during space missions.
  10. Our ultimate goal is to make long-duration space missions safer and support future human exploration of the Moon and Mars.
